methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mpeg -vn -c:a libmp3lame output.mp3.
methods.limits: The build needs libmp3lame (--enable-libmp3lame); its b option sets the bitrate.

methods.steps: Install the optional FFmpeg library, open the source, choose File > Export Audio and pick MP3 in the Format menu.
methods.limits: The FFmpeg library imports audio from most video files that are not DRM-protected.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.webm -vn -c:a libmp3lame output.mp3.
methods.limits: The build needs libmp3lame (--enable-libmp3lame).

methods.steps: Install the optional FFmpeg library, open the source, choose File > Export Audio and pick MP3 in the Format menu.
methods.limits: The FFmpeg library imports audio from most video files that are not DRM-protected.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.wma -c:a libmp3lame output.mp3.
methods.limits: The build needs libmp3lame (--enable-libmp3lame).

methods.steps: Install the optional FFmpeg library, open the WMA, choose File > Export Audio and pick MP3 in the Format menu.
methods.limits: Protected WMA files cannot be imported through the FFmpeg library.

methods.steps: Open the GIF, choose File > Export As, choose JPEG in the file-type list and click Export; the JPEG settings dialog follows.
methods.limits: The JPEG export has a default quality of 85 and stores no transparency or layers.

methods.steps: Run magick 'input.gif[0]' output.jpg.
methods.limits: The [0] modifier picks the first frame; quotes keep the brackets from the shell.

methods.steps: Open the JPG, choose File > Export As, choose JPEG in the file-type list and click Export; the JPEG settings dialog follows.
methods.limits: GIMP accepts .jpg, .JPG and .jpeg as the extension; the export is a new JPEG encode.

methods.steps: Run magick input.jpg output.jpeg.
methods.limits: This re-encodes the JPEG; it is not just a filename change.

methods.steps: Open the TIFF, choose File > Export As, choose JPEG in the file-type list and click Export; the JPEG settings dialog follows.
methods.limits: The JPEG export has a default quality of 85 and stores no transparency or layers.

methods.steps: Open the image, choose File > Export, select JPEG in Format, and save the new copy.
methods.limits: The Format menu in the export sheet lists JPEG.

methods.steps: Run magick 'input.tiff[0]' output.jpg.
methods.limits: The [0] modifier picks the first image; quotes keep the brackets from the shell.

methods.steps: Open the TIFF; choose File > Export, set the format to PDF, and save.
methods.limits: The Format menu in the export sheet lists PDF.

methods.steps: Run magick input.tiff output.pdf.
methods.limits: The formats page lists TIFF as readable and writable and PDF as readable and writable, requiring Ghostscript.

methods.steps: Open the TXT, then choose File > Export as PDF.
methods.limits: TextEdit's page layout differs from this page's fixed grid.

methods.steps: Choose File > Create > PDF from File, change the file-type filter in the Open dialog to show TXT files, select the file, click Open, and save the PDF.
methods.limits: Layout follows Acrobat's settings.

methods.steps: Run pdftotext input.pdf output.txt; without the second name it writes the PDF's name with .txt.
methods.limits: Converts a PDF to plain text.

methods.steps: Follow the 'Extract all Document Text' recipe: open the PDF, join page.get_text() for each page with a form feed, then write the encoded text bytes to a file.
methods.limits: The recipe warns that the extracted text may not be in reading order.

methods.steps: Choose Tools > Text Selection in Preview, select text, use Edit > Copy, then paste into TextEdit and choose Format > Make Plain Text before saving.
methods.limits: Manual excerpt extraction, not an export of all pages.

methods.steps: Run texconv -ft dds -f BC3_UNORM input.png; add -m 1 if only one mip level is required.
methods.limits: The format must match the target renderer. Mip generation defaults to all levels.

methods.steps: Open the PNG, choose File > Export As, choose DDS in the file-type list and click Export; the DDS settings dialog follows.
methods.limits: The DDS plug-in has been part of GIMP since 2.10.10.

methods.steps: Run magick input.png output.dds.
methods.limits: The formats page lists DDS as readable and writable, with compression defines such as dxt1 and dxt5, and mipmaps.

mpeg.fact: MPEG-1 describes compressed moving images that may have accompanying audio and originated for digital storage media.

webm.fact: WebM is based on Matroska and documents VP8/VP9 video with Vorbis/Opus audio.

wma.fact: Microsoft’s WMA family includes standard, Professional, Lossless and Voice variants.

dds.fact: DDS supports compressed and uncompressed textures, mipmaps, cube maps, volume maps and arrays.

png.fact: PNG is a lossless raster format with indexed, grayscale and truecolor modes, optional alpha, and animation support in its current specification.

gif.fact: GIF uses color tables and timed image sequences; its transparency flag refers to a palette entry.

jpg.fact: JPEG standards came from a committee process begun in 1986; the familiar coding mode is lossy DCT.
.jpg and .jpeg name JPEG; JPEG does not store layers or alpha.

tiff.fact: TIFF is a tagged raster format developed by Aldus and Microsoft; its specification is associated with Adobe.
GIMP supports high-precision TIFF import and export.

pdf.fact: The format holds fixed pages with text, graphics and images; scan imagery is distinct from extractable text.

txt.fact: Plain text has no rich text formatting, and TextEdit supports opening and converting it.
